record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: For generic initial data for the Einstein Cauchy problem, can one prove or control the formation of a trapped surface, that is, a closed surface whose outgoing null geodesics are converging?

evidence.quote: The problem with the application of the second singularity theorem to the global existence of a solution of the Cauchy problem is that it is not kown how to control the formation of a trapped surface for generic initial data.

The initial 3-manifold M is non compact and contains a closed trapped surface S, that is there exists an open relatively compact set in M whose boundary S is such that outgoing null geodesics at points of S are converging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem for the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(\mathcal{M},g)$. An initial data set consists of a smooth 3-manifold $M$ together with a Riemannian metric $\bar g$ and a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(\bar g)-|K|_{\bar g}^2+(\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g}K)^2=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_{\bar g}K-d(\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g}K)=0.$$
Such data evolve, by the Choquet-Bruhat–Geroch theorem, into a unique maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development $(\mathcal{M},g)$ in which $M$ embeds as a Cauchy hypersurface.

A closed (compact without boundary) spacelike 2-surface $S\subset\mathcal{M}$ is called a closed trapped surface if both families of future-directed null geodesics issuing orthogonally from $S$ (the outgoing and ingoing null congruences) have everywhere negative expansion; equivalently, $S$ bounds a relatively compact open set in some Cauchy hypersurface, and the outgoing null geodesics emanating from $S$ are converging.

Problem. Identify a notion of "generic" within an appropriate function space of asymptotically flat vacuum initial data $(M,\bar g, K)$ (with $M$ noncompact) and prove a theorem ensuring that for generic such initial data the maximal vacuum Cauchy development contains a closed trapped surface; more precisely, give criteria on the initial data, satisfied on a residual / open dense / full-measure subset, which can be shown to imply (and thus control) the formation of a closed trapped surface in the future development.
artifact.category_tag: Trapped surface formation in general relativity
artifact.status_search_result: Christodoulou (2008, published 2009) proved that an explicit open set of regular characteristic initial data—encoded via the "short pulse" ansatz—evolves to a vacuum spacetime containing a closed trapped surface, resolving the long-standing problem of evolutionary formation of trapped surfaces from regular data. Klainerman–Rodnianski (2012) simplified and extended this result, and subsequent works (e.g., An–Luk, fully anisotropic mechanisms, Einstein–Maxwell extensions) have broadened the criteria. However, a sharp characterization of "generic" Cauchy initial data leading to trapped surface formation, in the sense of a control theorem on a generic class within the full Cauchy problem (not only short-pulse-type data), remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the formation of trapped surfaces (Klainerman–Rodnianski)
status_evidence.snippet: Gives a significantly shorter proof of a slightly extended version of Christodoulou's remarkable result concerning the formation of trapped surfaces in vacuum spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Trapped surface formation from regular characteristic data is established for an open set of initial conditions.

status_evidence.title: A fully anisotropic mechanism for formation of trapped surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Christodoulou's mechanism, allowing the incoming energy to concentrate in arbitrarily narrow angular regions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works extend but do not fully resolve genericity of trapped surface formation.

status_evidence.title: A scale-critical trapped surface formation criterion for the Einstein-Maxwell system
status_evidence.snippet: Provides scale-critical criterion for trapped surface formation in Einstein-Maxwell.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues into broader criteria for trapped surface formation.
